title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters can control event production tools
summary: The briefing accurately reports organiser-assigned access, rollout windows and organiser-based licensing. The control paths and commands are supported; a minor documentation discrepancy remains between the join-verification guide and the PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: In Teams, the organiser path is Calendar > town hall > View event > Manage event > Meeting options > Production tools > Who has control of production tools.
claims.quote: Select Calendar ... in Teams. ... Select a town hall. ... Select View event ... > Manage event ... Select Meeting options ... In Production tools ... select an option from the Who has control of production tools dropdown menu:

claims.claim: No API or events policy parameter is documented for assigning production controllers.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external presenters production controls Who has control of production tools admin policy Graph PowerShell. Opened Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy and Graph beta virtualEventTownhall, virtualEventSettings and onlineMeeting; no production assignment property.

claims.claim: The join-verification path is Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list, select Yes verify accounts or No verification needed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires external presenter identity verification.
claims.quote: To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP
claims.fix: Keep the documented call. Add this sentence to the row note and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps: 'The join-verification guide documents this parameter, but the cmdlet reference currently omits it and describes the events policy as still in preview.'

claims.claim: The large-audience control path is Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: The join-verification policy defaults to No verification needed.
claims.quote: No verification needed | None | This is the default value. When organizers with this policy create events, they can decide whether external presenters must verify their identity before joining.

claims.claim: Turning the scheduling control Off after an event is scheduled stops the user running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.
